key_insight: InterMimicGen shows that humanoid loco-manipulation can scale by making robot motion data and a tracking policy co-improve each other in a self-evolving loop. This turns sparse human-object interaction footage into executable robot demonstrations for whole-body skills.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge that human-object interaction data is rich but difficult for humanoid robots to use directly because it is sparse, diverse, and not robot-executable.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-capture human-object interaction datasets into a unified resource.
Retarget human motions to humanoid robot references while preserving whole-body coordination and hand-object interaction details.
Use a self-evolving framework where generated robot motions and a tracking policy iteratively improve each other.
impact: This matters because it provides a practical path to scaling humanoid loco-manipulation beyond hand-designed demonstrations. For AI/ML practitioners, it suggests a data-centric loop for turning real-world interaction data into better robot policies and better training motion at the same time.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
